refsect1.title: DESCRIPTION
refsect1.para: The ReadoutREST package provides NSCLDAQ based Tcl driven Readout programs a REST server that can be used to remotely control and query the Readout. This facility is normally used in conjunction with the NSCLDAQ DAQ manager facility to manage Readout programs as critical grams that require attention during state transitions.
The ReadoutRESTClient package, ass the name implies, provides a Tcl REST client library for the ReadoutREST server.

refsect1.title: OPTIONS
refsect1.para: Configuration options control how the REST client connects with the server. Note that each REST operations (public method call), performs service discovery, connects with the server, performs the request, gets the response and closes the connection.

Therefore the pre-defined configure method allows client code to dynamically modify the server options. Furthermore, this strategy supports the case when the server exits and restarts, potentially with a different server listen port, between requests.
Here are the options, their defaults and their meanings:

listitem.para: THe host in which the Readout program we want to communicate with is running. This defaults to localhost. Note, however that the use of locahost is not host portable. Please get in the habit of specifying a real hostname.

The user the Readout program you want to communicate with was run under. Defaults to the name of the person runing the application. This, in conjunction with the -service option below is used to translate the Readout's service advertisement into a numeric TCP/IP port number.
The name of the servic advertised by the ReadoutREST package in the Readout we want to communicate with. This defaults to ReadoutREST which is the default service name.

refsect1.title: PUBLIC METHODS
refsect1.para: Each of the public methods below performs a REST transaction with the server. This transaction includes service discovery (translating the -user and -service values to a numeric TCP/IP port number), connecting with the server to perform a REST transaction and unmarshalling any resulting JSON into reasonable return values.
The methods which are considered public are:

listitem.para: Attempts to start a new run. The resulting Readout state is returned. Note that this is not the same as the DAQ Manager's state. If a transition to active data taking is not permitted (e.g. data taking is in progress) and error is raised.
Ends active data taking in the Readout program. Returns the name of the resulting state.
Attempts to initialize the hardsware in the Readout. Not all Readout programs support this. Those that do not are expected to silently ignore the request. Data taking must not be active.
Requests the Readout program to exit.
Returns the current Readout program state.
Returns the currently set title.
Returns the currently set run number.

Returns a dict that describes the Readout's statistics. This is a dict with the keys cumulative and perRun. The cumulative key contains statistics over the course of the entire readout program while beginning a run clear the counters in the perRun statistics.
Each of the keys contains a value that is a dict which is identical, containing the following keys:
Number of triggers sent to the Readout.
Number of triggers that resulted in an event. This reflects the ability of some hardware (e.g. XIA modules) and some software to reject triggers resulting in no data.
Number of bytes read from the hardware.
Sets the Readout's title to the specified title-string
Sets the new run number to number.

refsect1.title: DESCRIPTION
refsect1.para: The ReadoutREST package provides a REST server to NSCLDAQ Tcl based Readout programs that adhere to the standard Readout command set. Clients can interact with this REST interface to both control the state of the Readout program and obtain status information.

The intent of this server is to support Readout programs that are run under the control of the DAQ manager subsystem, however, in fact, any situtation in which a Readout program must be controlled remotely is supported.

The server package (tclhttpd) used to implement the REST server divides the URL space recognized by the server into Domains. A domain is a URL prefix. Three domains are supported by the ReadoutREST package:

listitem.para: Obtains status and state information
Sets parameters (e.g. title or run number).
Controls the Readout.

refsect1.para: Before describing each of these domains, it's important to describe URL formation. Recall that a URL has the form http://host:port/path/to/resource. The host part of the URL is trivially the host in which the Readout program exporting the REST service runs. The port, in general, is dynamically assigned by the NSCLDAQ Port manager and associated with a named service advertised by the server, qualified by the user running the program. The default service name is ReadoutREST. This must be translated into a port via interactions with the host's DAQ Port manager. The top level of the /path/to/resource is a domain as described above. E.g. http://somehost:39998/status/state is a URL that (assuming the host and port are correct) within the /status domain that returns the program state.

Finally a bit on what the server returns in response to its requests. All reqplies are a JSON encoded object (mimetype application/json). THe object has two standard attributes and additional attributes that depend on the request. The two standard attributes are:

listitem.para: The status of the request. This is either OK or, if the server recognized the request but, for some reason, could not execute it (e.g. a request for an invalid state transition), ERROR
A human readable error message in the event that status was ERROR

refsect1.para: In subsequent documentation we will only describe the additional attributes each request can return if status is OK

refsect1.title: The /status Domain
refsect1.para: As described above, this domain provides state/status information. Requests are made using additional URL path elements e.g. in http://host:port/status/request-type, request-type is the request. Supported requests and the additional JSON attributes they return are:

listitem.para: Returns the Readout's state in the state attribute. This is a string that can be one of: idle, active, or paused.
Returns the Readout's title as the string value of the title attribute.
Returns the Readout's run number as the integer value of the run attribute.

Returns readout statistics. These are provided in JSON encoded objects that are values of the cumulative and perRun attributes which provide statistics over the lifetime of the Readout program or over the current (or most recent if the state is idle) run.
Statistics objects have the following attributes:
Number of triggers seen by the readout.
Number of triggers that resulted in events.
Number of bytes read from the hardware. Note that this explicitly does not include Ring item overhead or body header sizes.

refsect1.title: The /control Domain
refsect1.para: This domain provides the abilityfor the client to request state transitions of the Readout program. All requests must be POST requests and must have a POST parameter called operation that indicates the state transition requested. the returned JSON includes an attribute, newstate that provides the state of the program after the transition.
Valid values for the operation POST parameter are:

listitem.para: Not actually a transition. This operation is legal in the idle state. It requests that the Readout program perform what is normally one-time hardware initialization. This is not fully supported by all Readout frameworks. If not supported it is silently ignored (although the requirement the state by idle is enforced).
Begins a new run. State must be idle
Ends the current run, the state must be either active or paused
Always legal, this operation requests the program shutdown (exit).

refsect1.para: Note that while the state paused is recognized and END can end the run when the program is in that state, the REST interface does not fully support paused runs, in the sense that there is no mechanism to transition the run into the paused state.

refsect1.title: The /setparam Domain
refsect1.para: This domain supports setting Readout parameters. All operations must be POST operations and two post parameters are required: name, which is the name of the parameter to modify and value the new value to give to that value. Return data does not provide any additional JSON attributes.
The name parameter can be either title, in which case value is a new title string, or run, in which case value must be a new positive integer run number.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Python client for Readout ReST server.

refsynopsisdiv.programlisting:
from nscldaq.readoutREST import readoutRestClient
client = readoutRestClient(host, serviceName, readoutUser)

refsect1.title: DESCRIPTION
refsect1.para: FRIB/NSCLDAQ readout programs can be augmented with a ReST server that supports control from outside programs. This is used by the managed experiment environment's helper functions to control Readout programs it managed though it is general enough.
Readout program enable a ReST server by using the --init-script option to run an initialization script that contains:

The ReST server advertises with the FRIB/NSCLDAQ port manager. By default, the service it advertises is ReadoutREST, although the environment variable SERVICE_NAME can be defined to override that name. In the synopsis above, the the constructor is parameterized with: host, the system that's running the Readout to be controlled, serviceName, the actual service advertised by the Readout's ReST server and readoutUser, the user running that Readout. Note that unless you really know what you are doing, you should user your own username. Note that in Containerized enviornments, os.getlogin() does not work, so your scripts shoud use getpass.getuser() which works in containerized and native enviornments to get the logged in username.

The return value from all of the methods that interact with the ReST server is a dict. The server might accept or reject the request depending on the state of Readout and the request (for example attempting to start a run when the run is active is rejected). The status key is always present in the dict and it's value is either OK, which means the server performed the request or ERROR which means it did not. If the server failed to perform the request, the dict will have a message key which contains a human readable string describing why the server did not perform the request.
Some methods may set other key/value pairs in the dict. See METHODS where those per-method dict contents are described in detail.

listitem.para: host is the host in which the Readout is running. serviceName is the name of the service advertised with the FRIB/NSCLDAQ port manager by the ReST server in the Readout program. readoutUser is the username of the user running the Readout program. See DESCRIPTION for information about the service names that are used.

ReST/HTTP as implemented by this class don't use persistent connections but per request connections. Therefore you don't really know if you have a viable client until you perform a request. One typical approache is to construct the object then immediately execute the getState to get the run state. This will fail if the constructor parameters are incorrect and a connection cannot be performed.
Requests the Readout to start a data taking run. This is only possible if the Readout's state is idle See getState below.
Requests Readout to end the run. This is only possible if the run state is active see the getState method.
Requests Readout to perform hardware initializations. This is only possible if the Readout's state is idle See getState below.
Requests the Readout program exit. Use with care as this request is always honored.
Gets the current run state of the Readout program. The returned dict, on success, will have the key state which will have one of the string values: active, paused, or idle
Requests that the Readout program set the run number for the next run to newRunNumber which must be a valid non-negative integer. This is only possible if the Readout's state is idle.
On success, the dict returned will have key named run which will contain the current integer run number.
Attempts to set the title of the next run. This is only possible if the Readout's state is idle.

Tries to get the current run title. On success, the dict will have a key title whose value is the string value of the run. Note that the title placed in state transition ringitems is truncated to 80 bytes.

Requests the trigger statistics from the Readout program. On success, the dict returned will have two keys, cumulative and perRun which contain the cumulative trigger statistics and the statistics in the current (or previous run if the state is idle). The values of both of these keys is a dict that contains the keys: triggers the total number of input triggers. acceptedTriggers some FRIB/NSCLDAQ Readouts have the ability to software reject events, the value of this key is the number of triggers that were not rejected. In most cases this value will be the same as the acceptedTriggers bytes the number of byts of data acquired.

refsect1.title: DESCRIPTION
refsect1.para: This module contains a potpourri of functionality that is useful when working with readout programs in the managed experiment environment. These consist of:

listitem.para: Constant definitions.
Function to allow you to find the host in which a program runs
A class that provides a centralized state polling objects and a factory for getting instances for them (requires Qt applications).

refsect1.title: CONSTANTS
refsect1.para: These are held in named enumerator calld CONSTANTS. See the synopsis for an example that shows how to reference them. The constants are:

listitem.para: The number of milliseconds usually used to poll things. Can be used, e.g. to set the interval of a QTimer e.g.
The default name of the ReST service that ia advertised by Readout programs.

Returns the host in which a program is running. In fact this can look up any program in the manager database, not just readout programs. mgr_host is the host in which the manager server is running, user is the username of the account that started this manager. service is the service name advertised by the manager for its ReST service. Note that the module nscldaq.manager_client defines nscldaq.manager_client.CONSTANTS.DEFAULT_MANAGER_REST_SERVICE to be the default manager ReST service name. name is the name of the program to look up. Note that if the program name has not been defined IndexError is raised.

Getting a host name back is no gaurantee that the program is actually running. For persistent and critical programs, the experiment must have been booted to start them. Transient programs are unlikely to be running for very long.

refsect1.title: STATE POLLING
refsect1.para: It is not uncommon for Qt client programs of the manager to want to know when the system changes state. If not handled, properly this can lead to a proliferation of timer objects and a periodic cascade of requests for the system state.
rdo_utils provides a StatePollFactory that attempts to maintain StatePoll objects as singletons for any given manager host/usr/service triplet.

rdo_utils.StatePoller is a QObject that periodically polls a manager for tis state. It can be created on its own but it is recommended that StatePollFactory be used to get an instance instead so that they don't proliferate throuhgout your application.

The StatePoller provides the signal stateChanged which it emits when the manager servers's state has changed. stateChanged passes the new state name to slots that connect to it. StatePoller instances also define the method state which returns the state of the manager as of its last poll of the manager.
The static method rdo_utils.StatePollFactory.getInstance produces either a new instance of a StatePoller or an existing instance if appropriate. Its signauture is:

host is the only required parameter. It is the host in which the manager is running. user is the username of the account that started the manager. The default value None uses the current username. service is the ReST service that's advertised by the manager for that user in that host. If not supplied it defaults to the default ReST service name which should be correct most, if not all, of the time.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Eventlog configuration and global enable Model/View.

refsynopsisdiv.programlisting:
from nscldaq.readoutREST import Eventlog
evenglogConfigurationView = LoggerConfig() eventlogConfigModel = eventlogConfiguration.model()
eventlogGlobalEnableView = Logger() eventlogGlobalEnableModel = eventlogGlobalEnableView.model()
# We need to establishs controllers to complete the MVC pattern.

refsect1.title: DESCRIPTION
refsect1.para: This module provides two models and views related to event logging. The first, LoggerConfig and LoggerConfigModel provide the view and model for a set of event loggers. The second set, Logger and LoggerModel the view and model. for a global enable of event recording when data taking is active.

Both class sets assume that there is an external entity, a controller, that hooks the user interface to the data acquisition system being controlled and back to the model as that data acquisition state changes with respect to event logging.
Both sets of models and views assume that you are working in side the PyQt6 enviornment.

refsect1.title: Event log configuration LoggerConfig and LoggerConfigModel
refsect1.para: The view and modedl of the logger configuration assume that the system can have several event loggers active. These loggers can be selectively enabled and the characteristics of those loggers are interesting to users. Instantiating a LoggerConfig object automatically instantiates a LoggerConfigModel to supply its data. This object can be retrieved using the view's model
Within this model/view pair, loggers are communicated using a logger dict. This is a python dict that contains:

listitem.para: ring The source of the data logged (ringbuffer URI in FRIB/NSCLDAQ).
host The host in which the event logger runs.
destination Where the logged data goes (usually a filesystem path).

partial True if the logger is a partial logger. FRIB/NSCLDAQ provides for full loggers which maintain a directory struture and can capture metadata along with a run as well as partial loggers that just create a soup of event log files in the destiniation.
enabled True if the logger is enabled. The logger will record data if the global enable is enabled and the logger itself is enabled. This allows loggers to be turned on and off individually.
criticial True if the logger is critical. If a critical logger exists, the FRIB/NSCLDAQ managed experiment environmet shuts down the experiment (transitions to the SHUTDOWN state).

refsect1.para: The subsections below present the methods of, first, the LoggerConfig view and then the LoggerConfigModel model.

refsect2.title: LoggerConfig (view)
refsect2.para: The LoggerConfig provides a signal named enableChanged that indicates the user has requested a change in the enable state of a logger by interacting with its controls. Note that the view, itself, takes no action to change the internal state of the model, nor does it interact with a data acquisition system.
The view has slots that are connected to model signals, these will be described as if they were any other method.

listitem.para: Called as part of the construction process. The optional parent parameter provides an object that parents the constructed LoggerConfig view object. If omitted the object is created without a parent.
Returns the view's associated model. This is normally a LoggerConfigModel but really only has to implement the same signals and methos of that class.

This is a public slot that adds a new logger to the view. Note that loggers are identified by their destiniation path. The parameter is a logger dict as described prior to this list of method descriptions.
Deletes a logger from the view. The logger is identified by destination which must match the value of a destination value in the logger's dictionary. If the logger is not found, IndexError is raised.
Marks the logger identified by destination as enabled. If there is no matching logger in the view, IndexError is raised.
Marks the event logger identified by destinatino as disabled in the view. If no longger with that destination is in the view, IndexError is raised.

refsect2.title: LoggerConfigModel (model)
refsect2.para: This class provides the data that drives a LoggerConrfig view. The class provides several signals in the Qt sense:

listitem.para: loggerAdded(dict) Is signalled when a logger is aded to the model. The dict is the logger dict that describes the logger.
loggerDeleted(str) emitted when a logger is deleted from the model. The string is the value of the destination key of the logger dict for the deleted logger.
loggerEnabled(str) emitted with a logger is deletd from model. The string is the value of it destination key of the logger dict of the enabled logger.
loggerDisabled(str) emitted with a logger is deletd from model. The string is the value of it destination key of the logger dict of the disabled logger.

refsect2.para: The following methods are procvided by the LoggerConfigModel instances:

listitem.para: Returns a list of the logger description dictionaries that have been loade into the model.
Adds a logger to the model. The logger parameter is a logger descsription dictionary. This method also emits the loggerAdded signal with the logger that was passed in as its parameter.

Removes a logger from the model. The logger whose destination key matches the destiniation key is removed and the loggerDeleted signa emitted with destination as its parameter. If there is no logger with the specified destination an IndexError is raised.

Marks the specified logger as enabled. Enabled loggers will log data for runs when global event logging is enabled. The loggerEnabled signal is emitted with destiniation as its parameter. If destination does not match a logger IndexError is raised.

Marks the specified loggers as disabled. Disabled loggers will not log data during runs even if the global event logging enable is True. The loggerDisabled signal is emitted with destiniation as its parameter. If destination does not match any logger, IndexError is raised.

refsect1.title: The LoggerModel and Logger model and view.
refsect1.para: The event logging system is assumed to have a global enable. If the enable is true, then all loggers that are enabled will log event data from their sources to their destinations. This pair of classes captures that. It is assumed there is an external controller object that links the view operations to the DAQ system and changes in the DAQ system to the model.

Logger instantiations, creates a LoggerModel which can be retrieved via the model method. The Logger connects to the changed signal of its LoggerModel so that it can reflect changes made to the model. Note that since the model/view reflect a single boolean, the Logger is just derived from a QCheckBox. Its sole method is
model which returns the model it is reflecting.

LoggerModel is quite simple as well. It emits a signal changed when told the state of the global logger enable has changed and passes that new state as a bool parameter to slots connected to it. It as a single property, enabled with a getter and setter with the standard enabled and setEnabled method names. Invoking setEnabled will set the internal state as well as emit changed with the new state as an argument.

refsect1.title: DESCRIPTION
refsect1.para: The EventLog model and view manpage described a pair of models and views for configuring the event loggers in a system and managing the globel enable for event logging. These classes require an external controller to actually interface between the signals emitted by the views, indicating user interactions with those views, and the underlying data acqusition system environment.

The LoggerConfigController and LoggerEnableController classes in this module provide that functionality for the managed experiment environment in FRIB/NSCLDAQ. They are both intended, as are their view/model pairs to operate under the PyQt6 environment.
Once constructed and linked to their views, and the Qt event loop started, no futher programmatic intervention is required. The constructor parameterization for both classes is identical:
The parameter meanings are:

listitem.para: The view (which also contains) the model the instance needs to interact with. This parameter is mandatory.
The host in which the manager server is running. This parameter is mandatory.

If provided, this optional parameter specifies the username of the user that started the manager server. If omitted or None, the function getpass.getuser() is used to obtain the username of the logged in user.
This optional parameter, if present, specifies the service the manager server advertises with the FRIB/NSCLDAQ port manager. If omitted, it defaults to the service the manager normally advertises.
This optional parameter, if present, sets the parent of the QObject that the controllers are derived from.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Model and view for statistics from a Readout

refsynopsisdiv.programlisting:
from nscldaq.readoutREST import ReadoutStatistics
view = ReadoutRestStatistics.RunStatistics() model = view.model()

refsect1.title: DESCRIPTION
refsect1.para: Readout programs in FRIB/NSCLDAQ maintain both per run and cumulative trigger statistics. The RunStatistics view class in this module provides a tabular view of these statistics. In fact, it is derived from QTableView from PyQt6. The RunStatisticsModel derived from QStandardItemModel provides the model for that view. The view of statistics is readonly so no additional signals are defined other than those the base classes emit.
The MV pair rely on an external controller object to maintain the model statistics. This makes them only dependent on the ability to get the required trigger statistics from a Readout program.

The representation of triger statistics provided to the outside world by RunStatisticsModel is a dict with the keys perRun and cumulative The values of these keys are dicts desribing the per run and cumulative trigger statistics respectively. These dicts have the same set of keys:

listitem.para: Number of triggers seen by the readout. This might be live triggers depending on the type of Readout.
The number of triggers that resulted in an event.
Number of bytes of event data emitted.

refsect1.para: The RunStatistics exports only the methods that QTableView exports. Construction takes the usual optional parent that default to none. The MODEL METHODS below describes the methods the model exports in addition to the QStandardItemModel methods. Under normal circumstances clients will only need the methods described below.

refsect1.title: MODEL METHODS
refsect1.para: The interface provided to RunStatistics is much simpler than the direct QStandardItemModel interface. A single poperty, statistics is defined which is a dict of the form described in DESCRIPTION above.
The statistics method, therefore returns the current statistics dict

Allows a new set of statistics to be loaded into the model. statistics_dict is a new statistics dict of the form documented in the DESCRIPTION section. The model takes care of updating the QStandardItemModel appropriately.

refsect1.title: DESCRIPTION
refsect1.para: (3python)ReadoutStatitistcs described model and view classes for maintaining and displaying the trigger statistics from a Readout program. Those two classes require a controller to actually gather the statistics from a Readout program and maintain the model.

ReadoutStatisticsCOntroller provides that functionality for the managed experiment environment in FRIB/NSCLDAQ. It polls the ReST server of a Readout program periodocally and updates the model associated with the view from the data it obtains.
The construction __init__ method has the following signature:
Where:

listitem.para: Is the view whose model the controller will maintain.

Is the name of the readout program as defined in the manager's database. Note that if the readout program was defined with the Readout Wizard, it will be the name of the Readout chosen with _readout appended to it.
The host in which the manager server is running.
The service advertised with the FRIB/NSCLDAQ port manager by the manager server for its ReST interface. If not supplied, the default value used by the manager is used.
The service advertised by the Readout with the FRIB/NSCLDAQ port manager for its ReST server. If not supplied this is the default value.
The parent QObject for the controller. If not supplied, this defaults to None which leaves the controller unparented.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Model and view for status of all readouts.

refsynopsisdiv.programlisting:
from nscldaq.readoutREST import ReadoutStatus
view = ReadoutStatus.ReadoutStatus() model = view.model() # A ReadoutStatus.ReadoutStatusModel object

refsect1.title: DESCRIPTION
refsect1.para: A data acquisition system may have several readout programs. This Model/View pair provides a means to view the readouts, where they run, if they are currently active and their run state.

Instantiating the view (ReadoutStatus) creates and associates a model object (ReadoutStatusModel) object so, in general, you don't need to directly instantiate one as the view's model will fetch it for you.

The currnet implementation of this MV is as a QTableView and associated extended QStandardItemModel. However the model provides a higher level interface for describing the data than the base class does. The set of readouts is descdribed by a list of dicts. Each dict describing a single readout with the keys:

listitem.para: A name given to the readout program. This should be unique.
Which system the Readout should run in.
Boolean that is true if the Readout is running.
Textual run state of the readout (e.g. active if taking data). If active is not true, typically this should be set to unresponsive

refsect1.para: The model and signal don't expose any additional signals other than those of their base classes. See MODEL METHODS for methods that are considered public in ReadoutStatusModel

refsect1.title: MODEL METHODS
refsect1.para: Note that these are all instance methods and the self is omitted for brevity.

listitem.para: Called implicitly when contructing an instance. parent is the optional parent QOBject. If omitted, the model is unparented. Note that usually a ReadoutStatistics view is responsible for constructing instances, however it is certainly possible to construct it to supply data for some other custom view type.
Called intially to initialize the model and load its data. readouts is the list of dicts describing the readouts.

Once initial data are loaded into the model, update can be used to update the active and state elements of existing items in the model. If Readouts have disappeared, load must be used instead. readouts is the list of readout description dicts.

refnamediv.refpurpose: A control panel for the managed experiment environment

refsect1.title: DESCRIPTION
refsect1.para: This program provides a control panel for experiments in the managed environment. More than one control panel can be spun up at a time, allowing the experiment to be controlled from more than one physical location. Furthermore, since the manager server actually controls the experiment, it will continue in its current state if there are no control panels.
The top section of the control panel provides control over the requested next run number and title as well as the actual run number as known by the manager server.

The next section displays the the state of the system and aggregate readout state as well as the elapsed run time if the run is active. Below that are a set of three buttons that are enabled and labeled depending on the allowed state transitions of the system.

The left most button either boots up the experiment or shuts down all processes associated with the experiment. The middle button either begins or ends a run if that is legal. The right most button requests that the readouts perform hardware initialization.

The normal sequence of experiment startup is to boot the system and then do a HWINIT although that is supported any time the run is halted (in case attached intrumentation has been power cycled e.g.). Once the system is in the HWINIT state, runs can be started and stopped. The title and run number will be loaded from the editable parts of the top set of controls.

Note that if event recording is enabled, the control panel will increment the requested and actual run numbers when the run ends. This is done in a manner that supports multiple control panels consistently.

Below the state management/status region are controls that support taking data over a timed run. Note that timed runs are not part of the server, therefore, the duration and the fact that the run is timed, is local to the control panel that has enabled this. This can be confusing if one control panel has enabled a timed run and another, that has not starts the run, as the panel that's enabled timed runs will, end the run after the requested duration.

The bottom part of the control panel is a tabbed notebook that provides:
A tab labeled EventLogging. This tab, when selected displays the set of event loggers and provides contrls to or disable them individually.
A tab labeled Readout Summary that, when selected displays a list of all Readout programs and their status. See the section READOUT DESCRIPTION FILE for a description of how these are defined and made known to the program.
One tab for each readout program labeled with its name. Those tabs provide trigger statistics for each program.

refsect1.title: READOUT DESCRIPTION FILE
refsect1.para: The readout_description_file parameter to the program is the path to a file that describes the readout programs. This is required because while there is a wizard you can use to define/describe Readout programs to the managed experiment environment, once described, there is nothing to distinguish them from any other critical program. If you have used the wizard to create a Readout, the Readout program itself will have the name yourname_readout where yourname is the name you gave to the Readout definition wizard.

The readout description file is a comma separated field file (CSV) each line of the file describes one readout program. The first, and manadatory, field is the name of the program as known by the manager. The second, optional, field provides the name of the ReST service that will be advertised by that Readout program. If not provided, the default value of ReadoutREST will be used to locate the port used by that Readout to provide its ReST control service.

This file defines two readout programs (presumably the experiment has configured an event builder to glue the events from these two together). The managed experiment database describes where the two Readouts will run and the environment in which they will be run. The first readout program is named Readoutone_readout and advertises the default ReST service name of ReadoutREST. The second readout program is named Readouttwo_readout and advertises its ReST service with the port manager with the name MyService Using differing service names for each readout supports the use case when one system must run more than one Readout.
